title: Transfer of Training Gains in Agentic Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: A Critical Review and Evidence Map
content: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve tool-using large language model agents, but target performance does not establish whether a training advantage survives deployment changes. This critical review separates target scores, target advantages over a comparator, and changes in those advantages. A purposive evidence map contains one registered comparison from each of 183 studies, including 57 four-score contrasts; it is not an exhaustive or prevalence sample. The synthesis identifies five distinctions that change interpretation: absolute performance versus relative advantage, harness-specific versus general gain changes, comparator identity, functional versus compositional and interface holdouts, and success coverage versus repeated reliability. We connect these distinctions to explicit source comparisons rather than pooling heterogeneous effects. A 24-study source audit and a new source-only duplicate AI extraction of 16 key studies expose uncertainty in exposure, resources, measurement, and coding. The companion records provide the complete 183-study bibliography, all 57 current four-score contrasts, target-level data, and coding disagreements. Evidence supports training advantages in particular deployments, but no general retention rate or universal advantage of multi-harness training. Crossed policy-harness evaluations, controlled tool holdouts, and calibrated simulation-to-real scoring are proposed to distinguish the remaining explanations.
